questions.q: What term is used in mathematics to describe the numerical measure of the likelihood that an event will occur?
What is the numerical value assigned to the probability of an event that is completely impossible?
If you toss a fair, unbiased coin once, what is the theoretical probability of getting a head?
Which of the following numbers can never represent the probability of an event happening?
A bag contains 3 red marbles, 2 blue marbles, and 5 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is red?
What do the sum of the probabilities of all possible outcomes in a sample space always equal?
A standard six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling an even number?
If the probability of a football team winning their next match is 0.65, what is the probability that they will not win?
A letter is chosen at random from the word 'MATHEMATICS'. What is the probability that the chosen letter is 'M'?
What is the term used for the set of all possible outcomes of a random experiment?
A box contains cards numbered 1 to 20. If a card is drawn at random, what is the probability that the number is a multiple of 4?
Which of the following describes an event with a probability of 1?
Two fair coins are tossed simultaneously. What is the probability of getting two heads?
In a class of 40 students, 15 are girls. If a student is chosen at random to represent the class, what is the probability that the student is a boy?
A spinner is divided into 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability that the pointer lands on a prime number?
If an event has a probability of 0.05, how would you best describe its chance of occurring?
A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 playing cards. What is the probability of drawing a red face card (Jack, Queen, or King)?
A bag has 4 white balls and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn successively without replacement. What is the probability that both balls are black?
What is experimental (empirical) probability based on?
a: Actual trials, experiments, or historical data

questions.q: If a weather forecast states there is a 75% chance of rain tomorrow, what is the probability that it will not rain expressed as a fraction in simplest form?
A die is rolled 60 times in an experiment, and the number 5 appears 12 times. What is the relative frequency (experimental probability) of rolling a 5?
What is the probability of drawing a spade from a standard deck of 52 playing cards?
A box contains 5 defective bulbs and 25 good bulbs. If one bulb is tested at random, what is the probability that it is defective?
Which of the following pairs of events are mutually exclusive when rolling a single die?
a: Rolling an even number and rolling a prime number
Rolling a number greater than 4 and rolling an odd number
Rolling a multiple of 3 and rolling an even number
Rolling a number less than 3 and rolling an even number

questions.q: What is the probability of selecting a weekend day (Saturday or Sunday) at random from the days of the week?
If the odds in favour of an event happening are 3 to 2, what is the probability that the event occurs?
A jar contains 4 red, 3 green, and 5 yellow sweets. If two sweets are drawn at random with replacement, what is the probability that both are yellow?
When tossing three fair coins at the same time, how many total possible outcomes are in the sample space?
What is the probability that a leap year chosen at random has 53 Sundays?
A bag contains integers from 1 to 50 inclusive. One integer is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is a square number (e.g., 1, 4, 9...)?
Two dice are rolled together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers showing on the two dice is 7?
Why do lottery games have extremely low probabilities of winning for individual ticket holders?
a: Because the prize money is small
Because the number of possible combinations in the sample space is extremely large

questions.q: If P(A) = 0.35, P(B) = 0.45, and A and B are mutually exclusive events, what is P(A or B)?
A bag holds 6 red discs and 4 blue discs. Two discs are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that the first is red and the second is blue?
If you roll a fair die 300 times, approximately how many times would you expect to roll a number greater than 4?
Which term describes events that have the exact same probability of occurring?
A letter is selected at random from the alphabet (26 letters). What is the probability that it is a vowel (A, E, I, O, U)?
What is the probability of an event whose odds against it are 4 to 1?
A drawer contains 4 black socks and 4 white socks mixed up. If you pull out 2 socks blindly in the dark, what is the minimum number you must pull to guarantee you have at least one matching pair?
If event A and event B are independent, how do you calculate the probability that both A and B occur (P(A and B))?
